correctness.rationale: For distinct \(a_i,a_j\), their signatures are \(S_B\setminus\{b_i\}\) and \(S_B\setminus\{b_j\}\); omitting both \(b_i\) and \(b_j\) makes them equal, so at most one \(B\)-vertex can be omitted, and symmetrically at most one \(A\)-vertex can be omitted. Conversely, those sidewise inequalities give at least two selected vertices per side for \(n\ge3\), hence nonempty signatures; a selected \(b_i\) or \(b_j\) separates every same-side \(a\)-pair, the symmetric argument handles \(B\), and cross-side signatures are nonempty subsets of disjoint sides. Enumeration then factors as \(\bigl(z^n+n z^{n-1}\bigr)^2\). The packaged checker exhaustively confirms the definition and coefficients for \(3\le n\le8\); the finite check is not used for the infinite proof.

The chain-graph algorithmic theorem is structurally inapplicable.

originality.rationale: Statement-level comparison found no source that gives the crown-family if-and-only-if criterion, complete cardinality enumerator, or all minimum-set classification. The foundational and 2014 general OLD papers were inspected in full text for the relevant families and the latter's main structural regimes were compared directly. residual_risks: No finite literature search proves global absence; an obscure source using another identification-code synonym could exist.

The scalar \(n=3\) case \(\operatorname{Cr}_3\cong C_6\) may be recoverable from cycle-specific OLD literature; the retained novelty assessment is for the uniform crown if-and-only-if classification, enumerator, and all-minimum-set count.

The 2015 conference paper's full text was not openly inspected beyond its public abstract and outline, so its inaccessible details remain a small residual risk; its stated chain-graph theorem is inapplicable to crowns.

value.rationale: The crown graph is a standard symmetric matching-deleted biclique, and OLD is an NP-hard identification parameter. The result does more than give one scalar: it classifies every feasible detector set, yields the exact cardinality enumerator and total count, and isolates a sharp sidewise rigidity rule. This provides a natural benchmark family and a reusable exact distribution for probabilistic or robustness questions about detector subsets; it is not an arbitrary finite slice or a numerical recomputation.
